candidates.title: FuseRAG: Fusing Structure and Evidence into Inference for Cost-Efficient Graph-based RAG
candidates.abstract: Graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) exploits relationships among evidence to support multi-hop question answering. However, conveying retrieved graphs through non-unique linear textual contexts to Large Language Models (LLMs) leads to graph-structure degradation and inefficient KV-cache reuse. Meanwhile, graph-structure order optimization is already NP-hard, and the additional KV-cache reuse objective further complicates the search by introducing potentially conflicting orders. To tackle these issues, we propose FuseRAG, a cost-efficient graph-based RAG framework that shifts most retrieved evidence from explicit textual contexts to latent representations. Our main idea is to separate reusable evidence content from query-aware structural interactions in latent space, while retaining only a few explicit facts as semantic anchors. The resulting latent representations are injected into decoder self-attention, where they reshape attention over evidence and thereby influence hidden states and next-token probabilities. This design preserves graph structure through latent interactions, enables evidence reuse beyond exact token-prefix matching. Experiments on three multi-hop question-answering datasets with Llama-3-8B and Qwen3.5-9B show that FuseRAG improves answer quality while achieving up to 2.7x and 2.2x TTFT speedups over the fastest graph-based baseline, respectively.
candidates.reason: グラフ型RAGで検索グラフをテキスト化する際の構造劣化とKVキャッシュ再利用の非効率に対し、証拠内容を潜在表現へ移してデコーダ自己注意へ注入し、完全なトークン接頭辞一致を超えた証拠再利用を可能にすることでマルチホップQA推論のコストを下げる。

candidates.title: CoMPI: Coordinated Model Merging and Parallel Inference at Edge
candidates.abstract: Modern edge intelligence applications increasingly rely on multiple deep learning models operating under strict latency and memory constraints. However, the limited GPU memory available in edge clusters often leads to costly model switching and frequent SLO violations, particularly under bursty workloads. Several techniques are effective in reducing memory pressure from different aspects: model merging reduces memory usage on individual GPUs by sharing parameters across models, while parallelism reduces memory usage across GPUs by reducing redundant replicas. Since these two techniques operate in orthogonal decision spaces, combining them in edge clusters offers the potential for greater memory efficiency. However, real-world deployments reveal implicit interdependen-cies between them, making independent optimization inadequate for realizing their combined advantages. We present CoMPI, the first framework to jointly optimize model merging and parallel inference in multi-GPU edge clusters. By reducing per-model memory consumption, CoMPI enables the deployment of more replicas across GPUs, enhancing system throughput under bursty workloads and mitigating SLO violations. It performs joint optimization by evaluating the parallelization scheme for each candidate merging scheme and greedily selecting the one that yields the greatest memory savings. To reduce the complexity of the search space, CoMPI employs a Binary Split Tree that recursively partitions candidate merging schemes and uses integer linear programming to compute optimal parallelization schemes. To accommodate dynamic workloads, it further supports runtime replica adjustment without frequent re-optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that CoMPI reduces tail latency by up to 142.7% and improves SLO satisfaction rates by up to 42.3% compared to state-of-the-art methods under real-world conditions. This work is publicly available at https://github.com/bigint405/CoMPI.
candidates.reason: 複数GPUのエッジクラスタでモデルマージングによるパラメータ共有と並列推論を協調最適化し、モデル当たりメモリを下げてレプリカ数を増やすことでバースト負荷下のスループット向上とSLO違反緩和を狙う並列推論フレームワークである。
